newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - NOV 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - NOV 18.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The government's economic policies go through their paces today as ruling party PASOK MPs and the party's Central Committee convene. The meeting is considered to be a test of the unity of the party, the first since PASOK was returned to power in the September 22 elections.

--The weekend's celebrations of the anniversary of the 1973 Polytechnic uprising - long an excuse for a night of rioting - passed peacefully this year, despite some small incidents between demonstrators and police.

--Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos vehemently attacks the United States' one-sided approach to imposing solutions in international affairs. "It is no more than a nightmarish body of international suzerainty and tyranny," he tells an international conference over the weekend.

--"Austerity and taxes will not bring growth," Xenophon Zolotas, the esteemed economist and former prime minister says. The solution lies in better management and exploitation of EU funds, the reduction and reform of the public sector and the release of the state from the yoke of failed public sector organisations and firms.

--Merchants and tradesmen will pay up to 25 percent more in taxes, if finance ministry plans to change objective tax criteria go ahead. Also on the cards are special provisions for border regions and sparsely-occupied islands.
--The Polytechnic breaks with the tradition of violent anniversaries with the help of a strong police presence and the guarding of the school's premises by students and teachers.

--Couples with real estate holdings worth more than 150 million drachmas will be among those forced to pay the new tax planned by the government for next year. Firms will be liable for the tax if they possess real estate worth more than 100 million drachmas.
--Justice Minister Evangelos Yiannopoulos says he will not consider decriminalisation of 'soft' drugs but felony charges will be reduced to misdemeanours and 600 users released from jail.

--The government's economic and income policies for 1997 will hit low and middle income earners as pensioners and workers get increases just meeting inflation or below it. New tax measures will also hit hard.
--Awards night at the Thessaloniki Film Festival sees a British and Spanish-US co-production walk off with the gold and silver 'Alexanders'.
